## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (77%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert

Blurred input (severity 3) is flagged, and InSitu cannot be excluded [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 77%, InSitu 20% | Moderate lead |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Two classes unseparated |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / OOD percentile 1.00 | Flagged: input suspect [F6] |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models pick different classes |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Invasive | Weak support [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Scarce glands; concept model links this to invasive [F2] · Weak
- **Atypical cells confined in ducts** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Low score; spot check only 12/20 [F3] · Weak
- **Benign stroma or fat** (regions 5, 7) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; points away from invasive [F4] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 4, 6, 10) · ↑ invasive · Above typical across three regions · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so unproven; this case also leans on Normal lobules (Unreliable, 0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Blur and atypical appearance (OOD percentile 1.00) distort features; the second model picks a different class.
- The true class is InSitu: it is in the conformal set at 20% probability.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 4, 6, 10** — Confirm pleomorphism and stromal infiltration; separate invasive from in situ.
2. **Region 11** — Are atypical cells confined within ducts, or infiltrating?
3. **Region 7** — Lowest-risk region (11%); check glands and benign stroma.
